Ergative alignment exhibits a person-based division. First-person pronouns do not combine with the oblique/ergative case marker. In contrast, second- and third-person pronouns, as well as nouns, do take the ergative marker when functioning as transitive agents. Furthermore, there is object-specificity conditioning; if the object is nonspecific, the verb becomes detransitivized and the agent does not carry the ergative marker.
